definition_en: the amount of space between two places or things, or a cool gap between people
core_image: 两盏路灯之间那段走不到头的黑
scene: 街这头看得见那头的灯，中间隔着一大段黑。She walked the whole distance without looking back.
sceneCN: 这里 distance 指「距离」（第 1 个义项：两点之间的远近）；句意是她走完全程都没有回头。

collocations.phrase: at a distance of ten metres

senses.title: The space between two points
senses.definition: the amount of space between two places or things
senses.definitionCN: 两个地点或物体之间的空间大小
senses.example: Measure the distance between the two posts.
senses.exampleCN: 量一量两根柱子之间的距离。
senses.why: Space becomes something you can count in steps.
senses.whyCN: 空间变成了可以用脚步去数的东西。

senses.title: The far part of a view
senses.definition: the place far away that you can see but not reach easily
senses.definitionCN: 看得见却不容易走到的那片远处
senses.example: A light shone in the distance.
senses.exampleCN: 远处亮着一盏灯。
senses.why: The eye stops at the horizon and calls it a place.
senses.whyCN: 目光停在地平线上，就把它叫作一个地方。

senses.title: A cool gap between people
senses.definition: a lack of closeness between people, or the act of keeping apart
senses.definitionCN: 人与人之间缺少亲近，或主动保持间隔
senses.example: A quiet distance grew between the brothers.
senses.exampleCN: 兄弟之间渐渐生出一种沉默的疏远。
senses.why: Two people in one room can still be miles apart.
senses.whyCN: 同在一间屋里，两个人也可能隔着好几里。

intro.en: Distance comes from Latin distantia, a standing apart, built on dis-, apart, and stare, to stand.
intro.cn: distance 来自拉丁语 distantia（相隔而立），由 dis-（分开）与 stare（站立）构成。

items.en: Stare meant to stand still and hold a position.
items.cn: stare 指站定不动、守住位置。

items.en: Dis- pushed the two standing points apart.
items.cn: dis- 把两个站立点推开。

items.en: Distantia measured how far apart they stood.
items.cn: distantia 量的是它们相隔多远。

items.en: Old French destance carried the measure of space.
items.cn: 古法语 destance 承接了空间尺度的意思。

items.en: English used it for space, then for time and feeling.
items.cn: 英语先用它量空间，再用来量时间与感情。

items.en: Today it covers miles, years and a cool silence.
items.cn: 今天它可以指数英里、数年，也指一段冷淡的沉默。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the stant stem, while the meaning group names other kinds of gap.
note.cn: 形近组共享 stant 这一段词干，近义组则是几个表示间隔的词。

equally far from two points

an empty space between two things

normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从两个站开的点开始，落到两个不再说话的人。

normal.en: Dis- plus stance: two standing points held apart.
normal.cn: dis 加 stance，就是两个站立的点被分开。

normal.en: The bridge is two kilometres away, a short distance by car.
normal.cn: 那座桥在两公里外，开车是很短的距离。

normal.en: A figure appeared in the distance and came closer.
normal.cn: 远处出现一个人影，慢慢走近。

normal.en: He distanced himself from the quarrel.
normal.cn: 他与这场争吵保持了距离。

normal.en: Old friends can drift into a polite distance.
normal.cn: 老朋友也会慢慢疏成客气的距离。

abstract.en: Picture two lamps with a long stretch of dark between them.
abstract.cn: 想象两盏灯之间拉着一段长长的黑。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler laid on a map, end on end.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子在地图上一段段量过去。

abstract.en: Picture two chairs pushed slowly towards opposite walls.
abstract.cn: 想象两把椅子慢慢被推向相对的墙。

examples.en: The distance between the two towns is forty miles.
examples.cn: 两座城镇之间相距四十英里。

examples.en: He distanced himself from the decision.
examples.cn: 他与那个决定保持了距离。

examples.en: A dog barked in the distance.
examples.cn: 远处有只狗在叫。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 distance 记成「站开一段」：dis 表示分开，st 与 stand 同源表示站，两个点站开，中间就留出了距离。

root: 源自拉丁语 distantia，由表示分开的 dis- 与表示站立的 stare 构成，本义是两个点相隔而立。英语先用它量空间，后来也量时间，再引申为人与人之间的冷淡与疏远。

sensesIntro.en: From a measured space on a road to the quiet widening of a gap between two people.
sensesIntro.cn: 从路上量出的一段空间，到两个人之间悄悄拉大的空档。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two lamps standing far apart with a long stretch of dark between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：两盏灯远远分开，中间拉着一大段黑。

branches.en: The first sense is plain measurable space.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是可以直接量出来的空间。

branches.en: The second sense puts that space in the far background of a view.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把这段空间放到视野的最远处。

branches.en: The third sense turns space into coldness between people.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把空间变成人与人之间的冷淡。

branches.en: Both senses describe a measurable gap, one in metres and one in feeling.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在说可量的间隔，一个用米，一个用感受。

branches.en: Both senses depend on a viewpoint that feels the gap.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖一个能感到这段间隔的视角。

intro.en: Distance sits in the stance family, where Latin stare, to stand, holds the whole group together.
intro.cn: distance 属于 stance 一族，中心是拉丁语 stare（站立），把整组词撑在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin stare, to stand, gives stance and distance; dis- makes the standing points separate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stare（站立）给出 stance 与 distance，前缀 dis- 让两个站立点分开。

items.exampleCN: 他们在门口站了一个小时。

items.example: The village is equidistant from both cities.

items.meaning: to get far ahead of others

items.meaning: the conditions standing around an event

definition_en: far away in space or time, or not friendly and not paying attention
core_image: 山顶的信号塔在雾里只剩一个模糊的小点
scene: 车开出很久，那座塔缩成雾里的一个小点。He grew distant after the argument.
sceneCN: 这里 distant 指「疏远的」（第 3 个义项：不再亲近）；句意是争吵之后他变得疏远起来。

senses.title: Far away in space
senses.definition: a long way from the place where you are
senses.definitionCN: 离你所在之处有很长一段路
senses.example: A distant hill turned blue in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 雨里远处的山变成了蓝色。
senses.why: The further a thing is, the fewer details it keeps.
senses.whyCN: 东西越远，留下的细节越少。

senses.title: Far back in time
senses.definition: happening a long time ago or a long time from now
senses.definitionCN: 发生在很久以前或很久以后
senses.example: Those are stories from the distant past.
senses.exampleCN: 那些是很久以前的故事。
senses.why: Memory thins the years the way fog thins a hill.
senses.whyCN: 记忆把年月磨淡，就像雾把山磨淡。

senses.title: Cool and not quite present
senses.definition: not friendly, or not paying attention to what is here
senses.definitionCN: 不亲近，或没有把心思放在眼前
senses.example: She gave a distant nod and left.
senses.exampleCN: 她冷淡地点了下头就走了。
senses.why: A mind can move far away while the body stays in the chair.
senses.whyCN: 人还坐在椅子上，心思却能走得很远。

intro.en: Distant is the Latin present participle distans, from distare, to stand apart, built on dis- and stare.
intro.cn: distant 是拉丁语现在分词 distans，来自 distare（相隔而立），由 dis- 与 stare 组成。

items.en: Stare meant to stand and keep a place.
items.cn: stare 指站着并守住一个位置。

items.en: Dis- marked the space between the two places.
items.cn: dis- 标出两处之间的间隔。

items.en: Distans described things that stood far from each other.
items.cn: distans 描述彼此站得很远的东西。

items.en: English used it first for places on a map.
items.cn: 英语先用它说地图上的地点。

items.en: It spread to years, relatives and cool manners.
items.cn: 后来扩展到年月、亲戚与冷淡的举止。

items.en: A distant look now means a mind somewhere else.
items.cn: 今天 a distant look 指心思飘在别处。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the same standing stem, while the meaning group gathers words for far and unfriendly.
note.cn: 形近组共享「站立」这段词干，近义组则是几个表示远与冷淡的词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a small point on the horizon and end with a mind that has left the room.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从地平线上的一个小点开始，落到一颗已经离屋的心思。

normal.en: Dis- plus stant: the two standing points are far apart.
normal.cn: dis 加 stant，两个站立的点隔得很开。

normal.en: A distant light on the coast means the harbour is still far.
normal.cn: 海岸上远远一盏灯，说明港口还远。

normal.en: Letters from a distant cousin arrived once a year.
normal.cn: 远房表亲的信一年来一封。

normal.en: His voice went distant when the subject came up.
normal.cn: 话题一提起，他的声音就远了。

normal.en: She seemed distant, as if listening to another room.
normal.cn: 她显得心不在焉，像在听另一个房间。

abstract.en: Picture a tower shrinking to a dot in fog.
abstract.cn: 想象一座塔在雾里缩成一个小点。

abstract.en: Picture an old photograph with faces too small to name.
abstract.cn: 想象一张老照片，脸小得认不出。

abstract.en: Picture a person answering a question a second late.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人回答问题时慢了一拍。

examples.en: The distant mountains were lost in cloud.
examples.cn: 远处的山隐进云里。

examples.en: A distant train sounded across the valley.
examples.cn: 一列火车的声音从山谷那头传来。

examples.en: He was polite but distant with strangers.
examples.cn: 他对陌生人客气而疏远。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 distant 记成「站得远」：dis 表示分开，stant 与 stand 同源表示站着，站得开，就是远的，也可以指心思离得远。

root: 源自拉丁语 distare（相隔而立），由 dis-（分开）与 stare（站立）构成，现在分词为 distans。本义是位置离得远，后来用于时间上的久远，再引申为人情上的冷淡与心思上的不专注。

sensesIntro.en: From a hill far beyond the river to a face that answers you from a great distance.
sensesIntro.cn: 从河那边很远的山，到一张仿佛从很远处回答你的脸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tower on a hill shrinking into a dot in the fog.
core.cn: 核心意象：山上的塔在雾里缩成一个小点。

branches.en: The first sense is simple physical separation.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是单纯的空间相隔。

branches.en: The second sense measures separation in years.
branches.cn: 第二个义项用年月来量这段相隔。

branches.en: The third sense measures it in warmth between people.
branches.cn: 第三个义项用人与人之间的温度来量。

branches.en: Both senses keep one thing out of easy reach.
branches.cn: 两个义项都让某样东西不容易够到。

branches.en: Both senses grow stronger the longer nothing is said.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是越久不开口，就越显得明显。

definition_zh: v. 使膨胀；肿胀；使扩张
definition_en: to swell or stretch outwards from internal pressure
core_image: 被越来越多空气撑得发亮的气球皮；用力时皮肤下凸起成绳的青筋；一只被填过平常刻度的袋子
scene: 气球皮被越来越多空气撑得发亮。Gas distended the balloon until the skin shone.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：气体从内部把气球撑大，皮绷得发亮。

senses.title: Swell from inside
senses.definition: to swell outwards because of pressure from inside
senses.definitionCN: （动词）因内部压力而向外撑大
senses.example: Gas distended the balloon until the skin shone.
senses.exampleCN: 气体把气球撑到皮发亮。
senses.why: A balloon skin pulled tight over more and more air.
senses.whyCN: 被越来越多空气撑得发亮的气球皮。

senses.title: Swelling of a body part
senses.definition: of a body part, to swell abnormally
senses.definitionCN: （动词）指身体部位异常鼓起
senses.example: The veins in his neck distended.
senses.exampleCN: 他颈上的静脉凸胀起来。
senses.why: A rope-like vein standing out under strained skin.
senses.whyCN: 绷紧的皮肤下凸起成绳的青筋。

senses.title: Widen a hollow organ
senses.definition: to widen a hollow organ or vessel beyond its usual size
senses.definitionCN: （动词）使空腔器官或管道超出平常大小
senses.example: The stomach distends after a large meal.
senses.exampleCN: 饱餐之后胃会扩张。
senses.why: A sack widening as it is filled past its usual mark.
senses.whyCN: 一只被填过平常刻度而变宽的袋子。

intro.en: Distend comes from Latin distendere, to stretch apart, from dis- plus tendere, to stretch; the same stretch root gives tend, tension, extend and contend.
intro.cn: distend 来自拉丁语 distendere「向四周拉开」，由 dis- 加 tendere「伸展」组成；同一个伸展词根也给出 tend、tension、extend 与 contend。

items.en: Latin tendere means to stretch.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tendere 意为伸展。

items.en: Distendere meant to stretch apart or swell.
items.cn: distendere 意为撑开、膨胀。

items.en: Distentus is the participle, stretched out.
items.cn: distentus 是分词形式，意为被撑开的。

items.en: English distend means to swell out.
items.cn: 英语 distend 意为向外鼓起。

items.en: The word becomes standard in medical description.
items.cn: 这个词成为医学描述的标准用语。

items.en: Distended and distension are common in clinical notes.
items.cn: distended 与 distension 常见于临床记录。

note.en: Distend is stretching apart from inside; its look-alikes share the stretch root, and its neighbours name other ways of growing larger.
note.cn: distend 是从内部向四周撑开；形近词共用伸展词根，近义词则是别的变大的方式。

definition_zh: 蒸馏；提炼；使滴下；（液体）渗出
definition_en: to purify or separate a liquid by boiling it into vapour and condensing it, or to extract the essential part of something
core_image: 蒸气在弯管里走一段，管壁上慢慢挂满水珠，最后汇成一滴落下
scene: 实验室里，学生加热烧瓶，蒸气在弯管壁上凝成水珠，最后汇成一滴滴进接收瓶。The apparatus distilled the mixture into two separate liquids.
sceneCN: 这里 distill 指用加热汽化再冷凝的方式分离液体（第 1 个义项：蒸馏分离）；句意为这套装置把混合物蒸馏成两种分开的液体。图中可辨识物件：烧瓶、弯管、水珠、接收瓶。

pos.zh: 蒸馏；用蒸馏法提纯或分离；提炼（思想、经验）；使滴下

senses.title: To separate a liquid by boiling and condensing
senses.titleCN: 用加热汽化再冷凝的方式分离液体
senses.definition: to purify or separate a liquid by turning it into vapour and then cooling it back into liquid
senses.definitionCN: 把液体变成蒸气再冷却回液体，以提纯或分离
senses.example: The plant distills seawater into drinking water.
senses.exampleCN: 这套设备把海水蒸馏成饮用水。
senses.why: distill comes from Latin distillare 'to drip down', so the verb describes vapour being made to fall as drops.
senses.whyCN: distill 出自拉丁 distillare「滴下」，这个动词描述的是让蒸气成滴落下。

senses.title: To draw a strong spirit from a mash
senses.definition: to make a strong alcoholic drink by distilling a fermented liquid
senses.definitionCN: 通过蒸馏发酵液制成烈性酒
senses.example: They distill the fruit into a strong spirit.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把这种水果蒸馏成烈酒。
senses.why: alcohol boils before water, so distillation is the classic way to draw it off, and the verb took on the trade.
senses.whyCN: 酒精比水先沸腾，蒸馏正是把它抽出的经典办法，这个动词便承接了这一行业。

senses.title: To extract the essential part
senses.titleCN: 提炼思想或经验的精华
senses.definition: to reduce a large body of material to its essential content, as if separating a clear liquid from a muddy one
senses.definitionCN: 把大量材料缩减为本质内容，如同从浑浊液中分出清液
senses.example: The book distills twenty years of research into one volume.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书把二十年研究提炼成一册。
senses.why: the laboratory operation becomes a mental one: what matters is what survives the heat of selection.
senses.whyCN: 实验室操作变成头脑里的操作：要紧的，是在挑选的加热中留下来的部分。

senses.title: To drip, of a liquid
senses.definition: to come out in drops, said of liquid falling from a surface or through a small opening
senses.definitionCN: 以滴状流出，指液体从表面或小口落下
senses.example: Water distilled from the roof into the gutter.
senses.exampleCN: 水从屋顶滴进排水沟。
senses.why: the oldest sense is simply 'to drip down', and it survives beside the technical sense.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是「滴下」，它与技术义并存至今。

senses.title: To form drops from vapour
senses.definition: to cause vapour to condense into droplets on a cool surface
senses.definitionCN: 使蒸气在冷表面上凝结成小水珠
senses.example: Cold glass distills the vapour into droplets.
senses.exampleCN: 冷玻璃使蒸气凝成小水珠。
senses.why: condensation is the second half of distilling, and the verb can name that half alone.
senses.whyCN: 冷凝是蒸馏的后半段，这个动词可以单独命名这一半。

senses.title: To reduce a text to its points
senses.titleCN: 从大量材料中提取要点
senses.definition: to shorten a long report or argument to its main points without losing the essential meaning
senses.definitionCN: 把长报告或论证缩到要点，而不丢失本质含义
senses.example: The editor distilled the report to a single page.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑把报告提炼成了一页。
senses.why: a text is treated like a mixture: the water goes, the flavour stays.
senses.whyCN: 文本被当作混合物：水走了，味道留下。

senses.title: To purify by removing the rest
senses.definition: to purify a substance by leaving behind whatever does not vaporize at the chosen temperature
senses.definitionCN: 把在所选温度下不汽化的东西留下，从而提纯物质
senses.example: The process distills the oil until it is clear.
senses.exampleCN: 这个过程把油蒸馏到清澈为止。
senses.why: purity in distillation is not added but subtracted: everything else is left in the flask.
senses.whyCN: 蒸馏中的纯度不是加上去的，而是减出来的：其余一切都留在烧瓶里。

senses.title: To keep the core and drop the rest
senses.definition: used figuratively of any act of keeping what is essential and letting the incidental go
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指任何保留本质、放走偶然成分的行为
senses.example: Good teaching distills a subject without thinning it.
senses.exampleCN: 好的教学把一门学问提炼，却不把它冲淡。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps both parts of the image: heat selects, and condensation preserves.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留意象的两半：火负责挑选，冷凝负责保存。

intro.en: Distill comes from Latin distillare 'to drip down', from de- 'down' plus stillare 'to drip', from stilla 'a drop'. English has used the verb since the fourteenth century, with the British spelling distil. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: distill 来自拉丁 distillare「滴下」，由 de-「向下」加 stillare「滴」构成，后者出自 stilla「一滴」。英语自十四世纪使用这个动词，英式拼写为 distil。年代均为约数。

items.en: Stilla meant 'a drop', and its deeper origin is not established; any older root proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: stilla 意为「一滴」，其更深来源没有定论，为其提出的更古老词根属于重构。

items.en: Stillare 'to drip' described liquid falling drop by drop, a plain physical verb before it became a technical one.
items.cn: stillare「滴」描述液体一滴一滴落下，在成为技术词之前是一个朴素的实体动词。

items.en: De- 'down' plus stillare gave distillare 'to drip down', which alchemists used for vapour collected as drops.
items.cn: de-「向下」加 stillare 构成 distillare「滴下」，炼金术士用它指把蒸气以滴状收集。

items.en: English distill appears in the fourteenth century for both the dripping and the apparatus, and the spelling distil is usual in British usage.
items.cn: 英语 distill 在十四世纪同时指滴落与器具，英式用法通常拼作 distil。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the verb was used for extracting the essence of writing and experience, not only of liquids.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，这个动词已用于提取写作与经验的精华，不只用于液体。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin origin of stilla is unsettled, so any root offered for it is a reconstruction rather than a demonstrated form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：stilla 在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论，为其提出的任何词根都是重构形式，而非已证实的形式。

note.en: Group one holds the noun and apparatus of the same family, which share the dripping root; group two holds verbs for taking an essential part out of something.
note.cn: 第一组是同一家族的名词与器具，共享「滴」词根；第二组是表示从某物中取出本质部分的动词。

entries.definition: The process or its product; the verb names the act that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 过程或产物；动词命名产生它的动作。

entries.definition: The vessel used for distilling; it comes from the same dripping root, not from the adverb meaning 'even now'.
entries.definitionCN: 用于蒸馏的容器；出自同一「滴」词根，不来自表示「仍然」的副词。

entries.definition: In- 'in' plus stillare: to drip an idea into someone, hence to implant it gradually.
entries.definitionCN: in-「进入」加 stillare：把观念滴进某人心里，因此指逐渐灌输。

entries.definition: The condensed liquid collected from the apparatus, named after the action rather than the action itself.
entries.definitionCN: 从装置收集到的冷凝液，以动作命名而非动作本身。

entries.definition: To take a substance out with a solvent or force; no vaporizing is involved.
entries.definitionCN: 用溶剂或外力取出物质；不涉及汽化。

entries.definition: To remove impurities and improve quality; distilling is one way to refine a liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 去除杂质、提高品质；蒸馏是精炼液体的一种方式。

entries.definition: To make something pure by any means, of which distilling is one.
entries.definitionCN: 用任何手段使某物纯净，蒸馏是其中一种。

entries.definition: To turn vapour into liquid or to make a text shorter; it covers only one stage of distilling.
entries.definitionCN: 使蒸气变液，或使文本变短；只覆盖蒸馏的一个阶段。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: De- 'down' plus stillare 'drip': the verb is 'to make drip down'.
normal.cn: de-「向下」加 stillare「滴」：这个动词就是「使滴下」。

normal.en: The family runs distill, distil, distillation, distillate, distillery.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 distill、distil、distillation、distillate、distillery。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical sense: distill water, distill alcohol.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术义：蒸馏水、蒸馏酒精。

normal.en: The figurative phrases mark the rest: distill the essence, distill into one volume.
normal.cn: 比喻搭配标出其余义项：提炼精华、提炼成一册。

normal.en: British spelling doubles nothing: distil, distilled, distilling.
normal.cn: 英式拼写不双写词尾字母：distil、distilled、distilling。

abstract.en: Picture dew forming on a cold pipe and running into a jar.
abstract.cn: 想象冷管上结出露水，流进罐子里。

abstract.en: Picture a long letter cut to the one paragraph that matters.
abstract.cn: 想象一封长信被删到唯一要紧的那一段。

abstract.en: Picture a muddy pond producing a glass of clear water.
abstract.cn: 想象一潭泥水变出一杯清水。

examples.en: The refinery distills crude oil into separate fuels.
examples.cn: 炼油厂把原油蒸馏成不同的燃料。

examples.en: She distilled the interview transcripts into four themes.
examples.cn: 她把访谈记录提炼成四个主题。

examples.en: Rainwater distilled through the canvas and dripped onto the floor.
examples.cn: 雨水透过帆布渗下，滴到地板上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「dis（分开）+ till（滴）」——让汽一滴滴落下、分开成分：蒸馏、提炼

root: 拉丁 distillare「滴下」= de-（向下）+ stillare（滴）；stillare 出自 stilla（一滴），stilla 更深来源不确定。英式拼写 distil。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one dripping: a liquid is boiled and condensed, a spirit is drawn off, an essence is extracted, drops fall, vapour condenses, a text is shortened, impurities are left behind, and finally only the core is kept.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一次滴落：液体被煮沸再冷凝，烈酒被抽出，精华被提取，液滴落下，蒸气凝结，文本被缩短，杂质被留下，最后只保留核心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: vapour travelling along a cool tube, gathering into beads, then falling as one drop.
core.cn: 核心意象：蒸气沿着冷管走，聚成水珠，最后落成一滴。

branches.en: SEPARATION AND PURITY: distilling separates by boiling point and purifies by subtracting what stays behind.
branches.cn: 分离与纯净：蒸馏按沸点分离，并通过减去留下的部分达到纯净。

branches.en: THE STILL TRADE: drawing spirits off a mash is the oldest commercial use of the same process.
branches.cn: 蒸馏行业：从发酵醪中抽出烈酒，是同一过程最古老的商业用途。

branches.en: REDUCING MATERIAL: extracting an essence and shortening a report both drop the incidental.
branches.cn: 缩减材料：提取精华与缩短报告，都在放走偶然成分。

branches.en: DRIPPING AND CONDENSING: the plain physical sense and the laboratory half-step are one movement of water.
branches.cn: 滴落与凝结：朴素的实体义与实验室的半步，是同一次水的运动。

branches.en: KEEPING THE CORE: heat selects and condensation preserves, which is what good distillation means in thought.
branches.cn: 保留核心：火负责挑选，冷凝负责保存，这正是思想上「好的提炼」的意思。

intro.en: Distill is a Latin verb of dripping, and its prefix and root also build the apparatus, the product and the word for implanting an idea.
intro.cn: distill 是一个表示「滴」的拉丁动词，其前缀与词根还构成器具、产物与「灌输观念」的词。

latinIntro.en: Stilla 'a drop' gives stillare and distillare; de- 'down' marks direction, and in- 'in' gives instill.
latinIntro.cn: stilla「一滴」衍生 stillare 与 distillare；de-「向下」标记方向，in-「进入」构成 instill。

items.example: The root names the single drop.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名单独的一滴。

items.example: The prefix points the fall downward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把滴落指向下方。

items.example: The Latin verb begins the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词开启词族。
他们把混合物蒸馏两次。

items.example: The unit distills a thousand litres a day.
items.exampleCN: 这台设备每天蒸馏一千升。

items.example: The plant is distilling the new batch.

items.meaning: a place where distilling is done
items.example: The distillery stands beside the river.

definition_zh: 蒸馏；蒸馏产物；提炼出的精华；（思想的）凝练
definition_en: the process of heating a liquid into vapour and condensing it to separate or purify it, or the essence extracted by such a process
core_image: 一锅液体在火上冒汽，蒸汽绕过弯管，在另一头凝成清亮的一滴
scene: 实验室里，烧瓶中的液体被加热，蒸汽沿弯管上升，另一端慢慢凝出一滴滴清水。The distillation separated the alcohol from the fermented liquid.
sceneCN: 这里 distillation 指加热汽化再冷凝以分离成分的过程（第 1 个义项：蒸馏过程）；句意为蒸馏把酒精从发酵液中分离出来。图中可辨识物件：烧瓶、加热器、冷凝管、接收瓶。

pos.zh: 蒸馏；蒸馏过程（可数或不可数）；提炼出的精华；凝练的成果

senses.title: Heating a liquid into vapour and back
senses.titleCN: 加热汽化再冷凝的分离过程
senses.definition: the process of boiling a liquid into vapour and cooling it again so that it separates from substances that boil at different temperatures
senses.definitionCN: 把液体煮沸成蒸气再冷却，使其与沸点不同的物质分开的过程
senses.example: Distillation separates a liquid from substances that do not boil at the same temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 蒸馏把一种液体与沸点不同的物质分开。
senses.why: distillation comes from Latin distillare 'to drip down', so the whole process is pictured as vapour falling drop by drop into a new vessel.
senses.whyCN: distillation 出自拉丁 distillare「滴下」，整个流程被想象成蒸气一滴一滴落进另一只容器。

senses.title: A single round of distilling
senses.definition: one complete run of the apparatus, often repeated to reach a higher purity
senses.definitionCN: 装置的一次完整运行，常重复进行以达到更高纯度
senses.example: A second distillation produced a cleaner sample.
senses.exampleCN: 第二次蒸馏得到了更纯的样品。
senses.why: a process that can be repeated becomes a countable event, which is why the word takes a plural.
senses.whyCN: 可重复的过程会变成可数的事件，因此这个词有复数形式。

senses.title: The liquid that comes across
senses.titleCN: 馏出物、接收到的蒸馏液
senses.definition: the condensed liquid collected on the other side of the apparatus
senses.definitionCN: 在装置另一端冷凝并被收集的液体
senses.example: The distillation was collected in a cooled flask.
senses.exampleCN: 馏出液被收集在冷却过的烧瓶里。
senses.why: the noun can name the product as well as the act, since the product is literally what the dripping produced.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既能命名动作，也能命名产物，因为产物就是「滴下来」的东西。

senses.title: The extraction of an essence
senses.titleCN: 提炼精华、浓缩要点的过程
senses.definition: the process of separating what matters from what does not, so that only the essential part remains
senses.definitionCN: 把要紧的部分与不要紧的部分分开、只留下本质的过程
senses.example: The essay is a distillation of ten years of fieldwork.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章是十年田野工作的提炼。
senses.why: the laboratory image of leaving impurities behind transfers easily to thought, where detail is the impurity.
senses.whyCN: 实验室里「把杂质留下」的画面很容易搬到思想上，那里细节就是杂质。

senses.title: The concentrated essence itself
senses.definition: the concentrated result of long experience or argument, reduced to its essential content
senses.definitionCN: 长期经验或论证被浓缩后的结果，只保留本质内容
senses.example: That sentence is the distillation of the whole argument.
senses.exampleCN: 那句话是整个论证的精华。
senses.why: once the act is finished, the noun names the small clear volume that carries the strength of the large muddy one.
senses.whyCN: 动作完成后，这个名词命名那一小份清液，它承载着大份浑浊液的全部力量。

senses.title: Industrial separation of petroleum
senses.definition: the large-scale process that splits a mixture such as crude oil into products with different boiling ranges
senses.definitionCN: 把原油这类混合物按不同沸程分成产品的大规模过程
senses.example: Fractional distillation divides crude oil into usable fuels.
senses.exampleCN: 分馏把原油分成可用的燃料。
senses.why: industry scales up the same principle, and the column simply makes many repeated distillations in one tower.
senses.whyCN: 工业把同一原理放大，分馏塔只是在一座塔里完成多次重复蒸馏。

senses.title: A shortened version of a longer work
senses.titleCN: 由长文本提炼出的简明版本
senses.definition: a short text that keeps the essential content of a much longer one
senses.definitionCN: 保留长文本本质内容的短文本
senses.example: The handbook is a distillation of the longer manual.
senses.exampleCN: 这本手册是那本更长说明书的提炼版。
senses.why: a summary is to a book what a still is to a fermented mash: the same content in less volume.
senses.whyCN: 摘要之于书，正如蒸馏器之于发酵醪：同样的内容，更少的体积。

senses.title: Memory keeping only the core
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：去掉杂质、只留核心
senses.definition: used figuratively of any process that slowly removes the incidental and keeps the central part
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指任何慢慢去掉偶然成分、留下核心部分的过程
senses.example: Memory works as a slow distillation of detail.
senses.exampleCN: 记忆像一场缓慢的蒸馏，把细节一点点滤掉。
senses.why: the abstract sense treats time as heat: what is volatile goes, what matters condenses.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把时间当作火：易挥发的走掉，要紧的凝结下来。

intro.en: Distillation comes from Late Latin distillatio, from distillare 'to drip down', built on de- 'down' plus stillare 'to drip', from stilla 'a drop'. It is recorded in English from the fourteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: distillation 来自晚期拉丁 distillatio，出自 distillare「滴下」，由 de-「向下」加 stillare「滴」构成，后者出自 stilla「一滴」。英语自十四世纪有记录。年代均为约数。

items.en: Stilla meant 'a drop', especially a drop of liquid; its deeper origin is not established, and any older root proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: stilla 意为「一滴」，尤其指液滴；其更深来源没有定论，为其提出的更古老词根属于重构。

items.en: Stillare 'to drip, to drop' turned the noun into a verb, used of liquids falling drop by drop.
items.cn: stillare「滴、滴落」把名词变成动词，用于一滴一滴落下的液体。

items.en: De- 'down' plus stillare gave distillare 'to drip down', which alchemy applied to vapour condensed and collected drop by drop.
items.cn: de-「向下」加 stillare 构成 distillare「滴下」，炼金术用它指蒸气冷凝后一滴一滴被收集。

items.en: Medieval alchemists built the still and named the process, and their Latin writings carried both into European languages.
items.cn: 中世纪炼金术士造出蒸馏器并为这一过程命名，他们的拉丁著作把器与名一并带入欧洲各语言。

items.en: English distillation appears in the fourteenth century for the apparatus and the act, and the figurative sense of extracting an essence follows by the nineteenth.
items.cn: 英语 distillation 在十四世纪指蒸馏器与蒸馏动作，到十九世纪出现「提炼精华」的比喻义。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin origin of stilla is unsettled, so any root offered for it is a reconstruction rather than a demonstrated form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：stilla 在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论，为其提出的任何词根都是重构形式，而非已证实的形式。

note.en: Group one holds the apparatus and the verb of the same family, which are often confused with the process; group two holds other ways of separating or purifying.
note.cn: 第一组是同一家族的器具与动词，常与过程本身混淆；第二组是其他分离或提纯方式。

entries.definition: To carry out the process; distillation is the process or its product.
entries.definitionCN: 执行这个过程；distillation 是过程或产物。

entries.definition: The vessel and condenser used for distilling; the noun comes from the same dripping root, not from the adverb still.
entries.definitionCN: 用于蒸馏的容器与冷凝器；这个名词出自同一「滴」词根，不来自副词 still。

entries.definition: The condensed product itself, as opposed to the process that made it.
entries.definitionCN: 冷凝所得产物本身，与制造它的过程相对。

entries.definition: In- 'in' plus stillare: to drip something in, hence to implant an idea gradually.
entries.definitionCN: in-「进入」加 stillare：把某物滴进去，因此指逐渐灌输一种观念。

entries.definition: Removing a substance with a solvent or force; it does not require vaporizing and condensing.
entries.definitionCN: 用溶剂或外力取出物质；不需要汽化再冷凝。

entries.definition: The removal of impurities to raise quality; distillation is one method of refinement.
entries.definitionCN: 去除杂质以提高品质；蒸馏是精炼的一种方法。

entries.definition: Making something pure, by any method; distillation is one route to that goal.
entries.definitionCN: 用任何方法使某物纯净；蒸馏是达到该目标的一条途径。

entries.definition: The change from vapour to liquid; it is one half of a distillation, not the whole process.
entries.definitionCN: 由蒸气变为液体；它是蒸馏的一半，而非全过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: De- 'down' plus stillare 'to drip': vapour is made to drip down into a new vessel.
normal.cn: de-「向下」加 stillare「滴」：让蒸气滴落进另一只容器。

normal.en: The family runs distill, distil, distillation, distillate, distillery, distiller.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 distill、distil、distillation、distillate、distillery、distiller。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the industrial sense: fractional distillation, simple distillation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出工业义：分馏、简单蒸馏。

normal.en: The apparatus is a still, and the same dripping root gives instill.
normal.cn: 器具叫 still，同一「滴」词根还构成 instill。

normal.en: The figurative phrases mark the rest: a distillation of ideas, the distillation of experience.
normal.cn: 比喻搭配标出其余义项：思想的凝练、经验的提炼。

abstract.en: Picture a long speech reduced to one sentence that still carries its weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一场长演讲被收成一句仍带着全部分量的话。

abstract.en: Picture muddy water entering a still and clear drops leaving it.
abstract.cn: 想象浑浊的水进入蒸馏器，清亮的液滴从另一端落下。

abstract.en: Picture a year of travel folded into a single page of notes.
abstract.cn: 想象一年的旅行被折进一页笔记。

examples.en: Distillation is the standard method for recovering alcohol from a fermented mixture.
examples.cn: 蒸馏是从发酵混合物中回收酒精的标准方法。

examples.en: The book is a distillation of interviews with two hundred farmers.
examples.cn: 这本书是对两百位农民访谈的提炼。

examples.en: Fractional distillation at the refinery separates petrol, kerosene and diesel.
examples.cn: 炼油厂的分馏把汽油、煤油与柴油分开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「dis（分开）+ till（滴）+ ation」——让蒸汽一滴滴落下、把成分分开：蒸馏、提炼

root: 晚期拉丁 distillatio「滴下」= distillare（滴下）+ -io（动作名词）；distillare 由 de-（向下）+ stillare（滴）构成，stillare 出自 stilla（一滴），stilla 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one dripping: vapour rises and comes back as drops, a run is repeated, the liquid is collected, an essence is extracted, that essence is named, industry separates fuels, a long work is shortened, and finally memory keeps only the core.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一次滴落：蒸气升起又落回成滴，一次操作被重复，液体被收集，精华被提取，那份精华被命名，工业借此分离燃料，长作品被缩短，最后记忆只留下核心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: vapour rising from a heated flask and returning as clean drops in another vessel.
core.cn: 核心意象：蒸气从受热的烧瓶升起，在另一只容器里变回清亮的液滴。

branches.en: THE PROCESS AND A RUN OF IT: one rise-and-fall cycle becomes a countable operation when repeated.
branches.cn: 过程与一次操作：一次升落循环在被重复时成为可数的操作。

branches.en: THE COLLECTED LIQUID: what drips into the receiver is the process made tangible.
branches.cn: 被收集的液体：滴进接收瓶的东西，是过程变得可触。

branches.en: ESSENCE: extracting the essential part and naming that part are two halves of one figurative move.
branches.cn: 精华：提取本质部分与命名本质部分，是同一次比喻动作的两半。

branches.en: INDUSTRIAL SCALE: a fractionating column is many distillations stacked in one tower.
branches.cn: 工业规模：分馏塔就是把多次蒸馏叠在一座塔里。

branches.en: SHORTER FORMS: a summary and a memory both keep the core and let the rest go.
branches.cn: 更短的形式：摘要与记忆都保留核心，让其余部分走掉。

intro.en: Distillation is a Latin verb of dripping plus an action ending, and the drip root also builds the apparatus and the word for implanting ideas.
intro.cn: distillation 是一个表示「滴」的拉丁动词加动作词尾，「滴」词根还构成器具名与「灌输观念」的词。

latinIntro.en: Stilla 'a drop' gives stillare and distillare; de- 'down' marks the direction, and -atio becomes -ation in English.
latinIntro.cn: stilla「一滴」衍生 stillare 与 distillare；de-「向下」标记方向，-atio 在英语中变为 -ation。

items.example: The noun supplies the single drop.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供「一滴」这一单位。

items.example: The verb describes liquid falling in drops.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描述液体成滴落下。

items.example: The prefix gives the direction of the fall.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给出落下的方向。

items.example: The Latin verb begins the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词开启词族。

items.example: The Latin noun matches the English one.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词与英语名词对应。

items.example: Distillation is repeated to raise purity.
items.exampleCN: 蒸馏被重复以提高纯度。
他们把这个液体蒸馏两次。

items.example: The copper still was heated slowly.
items.exampleCN: 铜制蒸馏器被缓慢加热。

items.meaning: to drip in, hence to implant
items.example: The teacher instilled a love of reading.
items.exampleCN: 老师灌输了阅读的热爱。

definition_en: easy to see, hear or notice, or clearly different from something else
core_image: 两条并排的白线，中间留着一道谁也不碰谁的缝
scene: 白线画得很实，边缘一点也不含糊。The two plans are distinct in almost every detail.
sceneCN: 这里 distinct 指「截然不同的」（第 2 个义项：彼此界限分明）；句意是这两个方案几乎每个细节都不同。

senses.title: Clear to the senses
senses.definition: easy to see, hear or notice, leaving no doubt
senses.definitionCN: 容易看见、听见或察觉，没有含糊
senses.example: There was a distinct smell of smoke.
senses.exampleCN: 有一股明显的烟味。
senses.why: A clear edge is what lets the eye rest on a thing.
senses.whyCN: 边缘清楚，眼睛才停得住。

senses.title: Clearly different
senses.definition: clearly separate and not the same as another thing
senses.definitionCN: 彼此分明，与另一物并不相同
senses.example: The two styles are distinct from each other.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种风格彼此截然不同。
senses.why: Two things stand apart only where one line is drawn between them.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西只有被一条线隔开，才显得分得清。

intro.en: Distinct is Latin distinctus, the past participle of distinguere, to separate, built on dis- and stinguere, to prick.
intro.cn: distinct 是拉丁语 distinctus，来自 distinguere（分开），由 dis- 与 stinguere（刺）构成，本义是刺出记号加以区分。

items.en: Stinguere meant to prick or mark with a point.
items.cn: stinguere 指用尖物刺或做记号。

items.en: Dis- pulled the marked pieces away from each other.
items.cn: dis- 把做过记号的几块分开。

items.en: Distinctus described what stood marked and separate.
items.cn: distinctus 描述被标记并分开放置的东西。

items.en: English used it for things clearly seen apart.
items.cn: 英语用它说清楚分得开的东西。

items.en: The sense of plain and unmistakable grew.
items.cn: 后来「明白无误」的意思壮大起来。

items.en: A distinct sound is both clear and unlike the rest.
items.cn: 今天 a distinct sound 既清楚又与众不同。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the stinguere stem, while the meaning group leans on clear edges and plain difference.
note.cn: 形近组共享 stinguere 这段词干，近义组则围绕清楚的边界与明显的差别。

entries.definition: to see or show a difference
a difference, or high quality
in a clear and unmistakable way
easy to see or understand
not joined or not the same
so plain that no one doubts it

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a sharp white line and end with two things that share no edge.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一道利落的白线开始，落到两样连边都不碰的东西。

normal.en: Dis- plus stinguere: a mark is pricked, so the two are kept apart.
normal.cn: dis 加 stinguere，刺出一道记号，两者就分开了。

normal.en: The bell gave a distinct ring across the yard.
normal.cn: 铃声在院子里响得格外清楚。

normal.en: Coffee and tea have distinct smells once you pause.
normal.cn: 停下来一闻，咖啡和茶的气味截然不同。

normal.en: Keep the two files distinct, or the proof is lost.
normal.cn: 把两份文件分开，否则证据就乱了。

normal.en: Her voice was distinct even at the back of the hall.
normal.cn: 即便在大厅后排，她的声音也很清楚。

abstract.en: Picture two white lines with a clean gap between them.
abstract.cn: 想象两条白线中间留着一道干净的缝。

abstract.en: Picture a knife cutting a sheet into two neat halves.
abstract.cn: 想象一刀把纸裁成整齐的两半。

abstract.en: Picture a mark pricked into a card to tell one from another.
abstract.cn: 想象在卡片上刺一个记号，用来认出彼此。

examples.en: There is a distinct difference between the two roads.
examples.cn: 这两条路之间有明显的区别。

examples.en: Each district keeps a distinct local accent.
examples.cn: 每个区都保留着自己独特的口音。

examples.en: The outline was distinct against the pale sky.
examples.cn: 轮廓在淡色的天空下很清楚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 distinct 记成「刺出记号」：dis 表示分开，stinct 来自刺，刺出一个记号，两样东西就看得出不同，也显得清楚。

root: 源自拉丁语 distinguere（分开），词干 stinguere 意为用尖物刺、做记号，加 dis- 表示分开。本义是刺出标记把东西区别开，因此既指界限分明、彼此不同，也指轮廓清楚、毫不含糊。

sensesIntro.en: From a mark cut to keep two things apart to an edge the eye can follow without doubt.
sensesIntro.cn: 从刺下的一道区分记号，到眼睛毫不迟疑就能跟住的边线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two white lines side by side with a clean gap that neither crosses.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条并排的白线，中间一道谁也不越过的缝。

branches.en: The first sense is clearness to the eye or ear.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是眼睛或耳朵感到的清楚。

branches.en: The second sense is clearness between two things.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是两样东西之间的分明。

branches.en: Both senses depend on an edge that can be traced.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖一条能描出来的边。

branches.en: Both refuse the blur that mixes one thing into another.
branches.cn: 两个义项都拒绝把一物混成另一物的模糊。

branches.en: Only the second sense needs a second thing to compare.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项需要另一样东西来对照。

intro.en: Distinct sits in the stinguere family, where one pricked mark gives several words for separating and for clearness.
intro.cn: distinct 属于 stinguere 一族，一道刺出的记号，生出一串表示分开与清楚的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin stinguere, to prick, gives distinct and distinguish; dis- keeps the marked pieces apart.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stinguere（刺）给出 distinct 与 distinguish，前缀 dis- 让做过记号的几块保持分开。

items.example: A distinct line divides the fields.
items.exampleCN: 一条清楚的分界线隔开两块田。
你分得清这对双胞胎吗？

items.example: The bird has a distinctive call.
items.exampleCN: 这种鸟的叫声很有特点。

items.example: The shape was indistinct in fog.
items.exampleCN: 那形状在雾里模糊不清。

definition_en: a clear difference between two things, or a high level of quality that earns respect
core_image: 两枚几乎一样的印章，边上一处小小的刻痕分出高下
scene: 两枚印章摆在桌上，只有侧面一道细痕不同。She makes a clear distinction between work and family.
sceneCN: 这里 distinction 指「区别」（第 1 个义项：把两样东西分开来看）；句意是她把工作和家庭分得很清楚。

collocations.phrase: a clear distinction between the two

senses.title: A line drawn between two things
senses.definition: a clear difference between two things or people
senses.definitionCN: 两样东西或两个人之间明确的差别
senses.example: There is a fine distinction between the two words.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个词之间有细微的区别。
senses.why: A line thin as a hair still keeps two rooms apart.
senses.whyCN: 一根头发丝那么细的线，也能隔开两个房间。

senses.title: High standing and honour
senses.definition: excellence that earns respect, or an honour given for it
senses.definitionCN: 赢得尊重的出众，或因出众而得的荣誉
senses.example: She won distinction as a young chemist.
senses.exampleCN: 她年轻时作为化学家就赢得了声誉。
senses.why: Work that stands above the rest is given a separate name.
senses.whyCN: 高出众人的成绩，会被单独给一个名分。

intro.en: Distinction comes from Latin distinctio, a dividing, from distinguere, to separate by marking.
intro.cn: distinction 来自拉丁语 distinctio（划分），源头是 distinguere（做记号分开）。

items.en: Stinguere meant to prick a mark into a surface.
items.cn: stinguere 指在表面刺出记号。

items.en: Distinguere set the marked things apart from the rest.
items.cn: distinguere 把做过记号的东西与其余分开。

items.en: Distinctio named the dividing line itself.
items.cn: distinctio 指的就是那条分界线。

items.en: English took it as the act of telling things apart.
items.cn: 英语借入时指把事物分辨开的行为。

items.en: The sense of personal excellence appeared.
items.cn: 后来出现了个人卓越这一层意思。

items.en: A prize, a tone and a fair argument can all show distinction.
items.cn: 今天奖赏、文风与公正的论证都能显出卓越。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the marking stem, while the meaning group offers difference and praise side by side.
note.cn: 形近组共享「做记号」的词干，近义组则把差别与赞誉并排放在一起。

entries.definition: clear and clearly separate
to see or show a difference
marking something as its own
the way things are not the same
a sharp difference set side by side
entries.definitionCN: 并置时显出的鲜明差别

entries.definition: very high quality

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a hairline mark and end with a prize given for standing above the rest.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一道头发丝细的记号线开始，落到因出众而得的一个奖。

normal.en: Dis- plus stinct: a mark is pricked, and a line appears.
normal.cn: dis 加 stinct，刺出一道记号，界线就出来了。

normal.en: The distinction between the two words is easy to miss.
normal.cn: 这两个词的区别很容易被忽略。

normal.en: She served with distinction in a hard trade.
normal.cn: 她在一个艰难的行业里做得很出色。

normal.en: A good teacher draws a distinction between error and laziness.
normal.cn: 好老师会区分出错和偷懒。

normal.en: The prize added another distinction to her name.
normal.cn: 这个奖又给她的名字添了一份荣誉。

abstract.en: Picture two seals on a desk with one tiny notch apart.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上一对印章，只差一道小刻痕。

abstract.en: Picture a hairline drawn across a page, still dividing it.
abstract.cn: 想象纸上一道发丝细的线，依然把页面分开。

abstract.en: Picture a medal placed beside an ordinary cup.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚奖章摆在一只普通杯子旁边。

examples.en: The distinction between the two senses is small but real.
examples.cn: 两个义项之间的区别很小，却真实存在。

examples.en: He served with distinction in the navy.
examples.cn: 他在海军服役期间表现出色。

examples.en: Critics praised the distinction of her prose.
examples.cn: 评论家称赞她文笔出众。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 distinction 记成「刺出分界」：dis 表示分开，stinct 来自刺，刺出一道界线，就有了区别，也指高出众人的那份卓越。

root: 源自拉丁语 distinctio，来自 distinguere（做记号分开），词干 stinguere 意为刺。本义是划出界线、把东西分辨开，后来从「分辨」引申出「出众」与「荣誉」，因为出众的人也被单独划了出来。

sensesIntro.en: From a hairline drawn between two words to the honour that marks one person above the rest.
sensesIntro.cn: 从两个词之间画出的一道细线，到把一个人标在众人之上的那份荣誉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two nearly identical seals, told apart by one small notch on the side.
core.cn: 核心意象：两枚几乎相同的印章，靠侧面一道小刻痕分开。

branches.en: The first sense is the line itself.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是那条界线本身。

branches.en: The second sense is the honour that follows being set apart.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是被单独划出之后得到的荣誉。

branches.en: Both senses depend on someone noticing a difference.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖有人注意到差别。

branches.en: Both can be lost when nothing is compared.
branches.cn: 两个义项在不作比较时都无从谈起。

branches.en: Only the second sense needs public praise or a prize.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项需要公开的称赞或奖项。

intro.en: Distinction belongs to the marking family, where one pricked line yields words for difference and for fame.
intro.cn: distinction 属于「做记号」一族，一道刺出的线，长出表示差别与名声的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin stinguere, to prick, gives distinction and distinguish; dis- keeps the marked pieces apart.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stinguere（刺）给出 distinction 与 distinguish，前缀 dis- 让做过记号的几块保持分开。

items.meaning: the dividing line and the honour it brings
items.example: A fine distinction separates the two terms.
items.exampleCN: 两个术语之间有细微区别。

items.example: She distinguished the two voices at once.
items.exampleCN: 她一下分辨出两个声音。

definition_zh: 独特的；有辨识度的；区别性的；特有的
definition_en: serving to distinguish something, or so characteristic that it is easily recognized
core_image: 一群相似的鸟里，有一只胸前的红斑独一无二
scene: 观鸟台上，一群人举着望远镜，指向一只胸前有红斑的鸟。On the birdwatching platform a group points through binoculars at a bird with a distinctive red patch on its breast.
sceneCN: 这里 distinctive 是「有辨识度的、独特的」（第 1 个义项：起区分作用的）；句意：观鸟台上，一群人举着望远镜指向一只胸前有独特红斑的鸟。图中可辨识物件：望远镜、鸟群、胸前的红斑、图鉴。

pos.zh: 独特的；区别性的；有辨识度的

senses.title: Serving to tell one thing from another
senses.definition: marking a difference that allows one thing to be told apart from others
senses.definitionCN: 标示出某种差异，使一物能与别的区分开
senses.example: The distinctive feature of the species is its curved bill.
senses.exampleCN: 这个物种的显著特征是弯喙。
senses.why: Latin distinguere is dis- 'apart' plus stinguere 'to prick'. A distinctive mark is a pricked line that separates one thing from the next.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 distinguere 是 dis-“分开”加 stinguere“刺”。distinctive 的标记就是一条刺出来的线，把一物与下一物分开。

senses.title: Easy to recognize at once
senses.definition: so characteristic that it can be recognized quickly and confidently
senses.definitionCN: 特征明显到能被迅速且确信地认出
senses.example: She has a distinctive way of laughing.
senses.exampleCN: 她笑起来的方式很有辨识度。
senses.why: Recognition is the practical test of a distinction. If the mark lets you pick the right one without hesitation, it is distinctive.
senses.whyCN: 认出是区分是否有效的实际检验。如果这个标记让你毫不犹豫地挑对，它就是有辨识度的。

senses.title: Belonging to one person or place
senses.definition: characteristic of a particular individual, group or region rather than of a whole class
senses.definitionCN: 属于特定个人、群体或地区而非整个类别的
senses.example: The valley has a distinctive microclimate.
senses.exampleCN: 这条山谷有独特的小气候。
senses.why: A distinction can be collective. The adjective then says that this feature belongs here and is not shared with neighbours.
senses.whyCN: 区分也可以是集体的。此时形容词表示这个特征属于此地，并不与邻处共享。

senses.title: A sound that changes meaning
senses.titleCN: 区别性语音特征（语言学）
senses.definition: in phonology, describing a sound feature that distinguishes one phoneme from another in a language
senses.definitionCN: 音系学中描述能在一门语言里把一个音位与另一个区分开的语音特征
senses.example: Voicing is a distinctive feature in English.
senses.exampleCN: 清浊对立在英语中是区别性特征。
senses.why: Phonology borrows the word for a formal job: if swapping the feature changes the word, the feature is distinctive; if not, it is not.
senses.whyCN: 音系学借这个词给一项形式化工作命名：若替换该特征会改变词义，它就是区别性的；若不会，就不是。

senses.title: A strength rivals cannot copy
senses.definition: in business strategy, describing a capability that sets a firm apart and is hard for rivals to imitate
senses.definitionCN: 战略管理中描述使公司与众不同且难以被对手模仿的能力
senses.example: Their distinctive competence is rapid prototyping.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的独特能力是快速原型开发。
senses.why: A firm survives by being separable from the crowd. Distinctive competence is the internal mark that makes the separation real rather than advertised.
senses.whyCN: 公司靠与众人可分开而存活。独特能力就是那个使分离成为真实而非广告说辞的内部标记。

senses.title: A mark that can be a trademark
senses.definition: in trademark law, describing a sign that consumers can use to identify the source of goods
senses.definitionCN: 商标法中描述消费者能借以识别商品来源的标志
senses.example: The court found the logo sufficiently distinctive.
senses.exampleCN: 法院认定该标识具有足够的显著性。
senses.why: A trademark must do the work of a distinction: tell this seller's goods from another's. Generic words cannot, so distinctiveness is a legal threshold.
senses.whyCN: 商标必须承担区分的工作：把这家的货与别家的分开。通用词做不到，因此显著性是法律门槛。

senses.title: Markings that identify an animal
senses.definition: in zoology, describing patterns or features by which individuals or species are identified
senses.definitionCN: 动物学中描述用于识别个体或物种的纹样或特征
senses.example: Each tiger has a distinctive stripe pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 每只老虎的条纹图案都独特。
senses.why: Nature supplies the marks that field guides rely on. The word moves from the observer's act of separating to the animal's visible equipment for being separated.
senses.whyCN: 自然提供了图鉴所依赖的标记。这个词从观察者的“分开”行为，转到动物身上“被分开”的可见装备。

senses.title: Having a character of its own
senses.definition: in design and criticism, describing a form that has a clear individual character rather than a generic one
senses.definitionCN: 设计与批评中描述具有清晰个体性格而非泛泛之形的形式
senses.example: The building has a distinctive silhouette.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑有独特的轮廓。
senses.why: Design aims at a shape you could pick out of a skyline. The adjective judges the result by the same test as sense 02: could you recognize it again?
senses.whyCN: 设计追求一个能从天际线里挑出来的形状。这个形容词用与第 2 义项相同的检验来评判结果：你能再认出它吗？

intro.en: Distinctive is distinct plus -ive. Distinct comes from Latin distinctus, the participle of distinguere, dis- 'apart' plus stinguere 'to prick'. The adjective marks whatever does the work of pricking out a difference.
intro.cn: distinctive 是 distinct 加 -ive。distinct 来自拉丁 distinctus，即 distinguere 的分词，由 dis-“分开”加 stinguere“刺”构成。这个形容词标记任何承担“刺出差异”这一工作的东西。

items.en: The root *steig- meant 'to prick, to stick'. It gives Latin stinguere and English stick, sting and stitch.
items.cn: 词根 *steig- 意为“刺、扎”。它给出拉丁 stinguere，以及英语 stick、sting、stitch。

items.en: Stinguere meant 'to prick, to extinguish'. With dis- it became distinguere, 'to separate by marking, to distinguish'. The image is a pointed tool drawing a line.
items.cn: stinguere 意为“刺、熄灭”。加 dis- 成为 distinguere“用标记分开、区分”。意象是一把尖工具划出一条线。

items.en: The participle distinctus meant 'separated, marked off'. The noun distinctio named a difference or a dividing. Both reached English through French.
items.cn: 分词 distinctus 意为“被分开、被标出”。名词 distinctio 指差异或划分。两者都经法语进入英语。

items.en: English distinct first means 'separate, individual', then 'clear to the senses'. The notion of clarity grows out of the notion of being marked off.
items.cn: 英语 distinct 初义为“分开的、个别的”，后指“感官上清晰的”。清晰这一观念正是从“被标出”生长出来的。

items.en: Distinctive appears in the 17th century as 'serving to distinguish'. It quickly extends to 'characteristic', since what distinguishes a thing is what we notice about it.
items.cn: distinctive 于 17 世纪出现，意为“起区分作用的”。它很快扩展到“有特征的”，因为使一物区别于他物的，正是我们注意到的东西。

items.en: Phonology adopts distinctive feature in the 1930s; trademark law and strategic management adopt distinctive character and distinctive competence later in the century.
items.cn: 音系学在 1930 年代采用 distinctive feature；商标法与战略管理在 20 世纪后半叶采用 distinctive character 与 distinctive competence。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the plain adjective, the noun of difference and the adverb. The meaning group contrasts distinctive with unique, characteristic and recognizable.
note.cn: 形近组区分普通形容词、表差异的名词与副词；词义组把 distinctive 与独特、典型、可辨认区分开。

entries.definition: clearly different or clearly perceived. It states separateness, while distinctive states the power to mark that separateness.
entries.definitionCN: 明显不同的，或明显可感的。它陈述分离，而 distinctive 陈述标记这种分离的能力。

entries.definition: a difference, or excellence. The adjective is built on the same participle.
entries.definitionCN: 差异，或优异。形容词由同一分词构成。

entries.definition: in a way that marks something out. It modifies the verb, while distinctive modifies the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 以能标出某物的方式。它修饰动词，而 distinctive 修饰名词。

entries.definition: typical of a person or thing. It says the feature belongs to the type, while distinctive says it separates from the type.
entries.definitionCN: 某人或某物所典型的。它说特征属于该类，而 distinctive 说特征使其脱离该类。

entries.definition: being the only one of its kind. It is absolute, while distinctive allows comparison and degree.
entries.definitionCN: 同类中唯一的。它是绝对的，而 distinctive 允许比较与程度。

entries.definition: able to be identified from previous experience. It describes the observer's success, not the feature's power.
entries.definitionCN: 能凭先前经验被认出的。它描述观察者的成功，而非特征的力量。

entries.definition: single, or having a personal style. It stresses separateness of being rather than the visible mark.
entries.definitionCN: 单个的，或有个人风格的。它强调存在的独立，而非可见的标记。

entries.definition: clearly noticeable. It measures strength of impression, while distinctive measures power to distinguish.
entries.definitionCN: 明显引人注意的。它衡量印象的强度，而 distinctive 衡量区分的能力。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to a prick that draws a line, then follow that line into birds, voices, sounds, brands and buildings.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词系在“刺出一条线”的动作上，再让这条线走到鸟、嗓音、语音、品牌与建筑。

normal.en: See stinguere, 'to prick': a distinctive mark is a line pricked out.
normal.cn: 看见 stinguere“刺”：distinctive 的标记就是刺出来的一条线。

normal.en: Test it by recognition: could you pick that bird out of a flock?
normal.cn: 用认出法检验：你能把那只鸟从鸟群里挑出来吗？

normal.en: For a voice, the mark is on the ear, not on the body.
normal.cn: 嗓音方面，标记在耳朵上，而不在身体上。

normal.en: In phonology, swap the feature: if the word changes, it is distinctive.
normal.cn: 音系学里，把特征换掉：若词变了，它就是区别性的。

normal.en: For trademarks, the test is source: can buyers tell whose goods these are?
normal.cn: 商标方面，检验是来源：买家能看出这是谁的货吗？

abstract.en: Reduce every sense to one question: does this mark let you separate it from the rest?
abstract.cn: 把每个义项缩成一个问题：这个标记能让你把它与其余的分开吗？

abstract.en: Notice that the word needs neighbours: nothing is distinctive in an empty room.
abstract.cn: 注意这个词需要邻居：空房间里没有东西是独特的。

abstract.en: Keep the double role: the mark both separates and attracts attention.
abstract.cn: 记住双重角色：标记既分开，又吸引注意。

examples.en: The region is known for its distinctive architecture.
examples.cn: 这个地区以独特的建筑闻名。

examples.en: Stress is a distinctive feature in English word pairs.
examples.cn: 重音是英语词对中的一个区别性特征。

examples.en: The brand's distinctive logo is protected by law.
examples.cn: 该品牌独特的标识受法律保护。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“地斯廷克提夫”：地斯廷克（distinct）一提，大家就认出是谁——distinctive 就是独特的、有辨识度的。

root: 拉丁语 stinguere“刺”，加 dis- 成 distinguere“用标记分开、区分”，分词 distinctus“被分开的”，加 -ive 构成 distinctive。同根词有 distinct、distinction、instinct、extinct、stimulus、stick、sting。

sensesIntro.en: Distinctive always answers one question: does this feature let you tell it apart? The feature may be a curved bill, a laugh, a valley's climate, a voiced consonant, a firm's capability, a logo, a tiger's stripes or a building's outline. The eight senses move across biology, language, law and design, but each describes the same power, the power to draw a line that holds.
sensesIntro.cn: distinctive 始终回答一个问题：这个特征能让你把它分开吗？这个特征可以是弯喙、笑声、山谷的气候、浊辅音、公司的能力、标识、虎纹或建筑的轮廓。八个义项走过生物学、语言、法律与设计，但每一个描述的都是同一种力量：画出一条站得住的线。

core.en: A mark that separates: the feature by which a thing is picked out.
core.cn: 起分开作用的标记：借以把某物挑出来的特征。

branches.en: PERCEPTION: a mark that separates and a mark that is recognized.
branches.cn: 知觉：起分开作用的标记，以及能被认出的标记。

branches.en: NATURE AND PLACE: features belonging to a region or an animal.
branches.cn: 自然与地方：属于某地区或某动物的特征。

branches.en: LANGUAGE: a sound feature that changes meaning.
branches.cn: 语言：能改变词义的语音特征。

branches.en: MARKET AND LAW: capability and legally protected distinctiveness.
branches.cn: 市场与法律：能力，以及受法律保护的显著性。

branches.en: DESIGN: a form with a character of its own.
branches.cn: 设计：有自身性格的形式。

intro.en: Distinctive is a participle plus -ive. The items show the stinguere family, where the same root produces words of pricking, of putting out and of being stirred.
intro.cn: distinctive 是分词加 -ive。下列条目展示 stinguere 词族，同一词根产生表示“刺”“熄灭”与“被激起”的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the verb, its participle and its noun. The idea of a pricked boundary is present in all three.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出动词、分词与名词。被刺出的边界这一观念在三者中都在。

items.meaningCN: 起区分作用的；有特征的

items.meaning: clearly different; clear to the senses
items.exampleCN: 出现了两个明确的群体。

items.example: Light is a stimulus for the eye.

items.structure: Old English sticca, from the same prick root
items.meaning: a thin piece of wood; to pierce or adhere
items.example: Stick the needle into the cloth.

latinEntries.meaning: to separate by marking; to distinguish

definition_en: to see or explain the difference between things, or to make yourself noticed by doing well
core_image: 两片相似的叶子放在掌心，先看边缘的锯齿，再看叶脉
scene: 两片叶子几乎一样，他并排举到光下看了很久。Can you distinguish the real note from the copy?
sceneCN: 这里 distinguish 指「区分」（第 1 个义项：看出两者的差别）；句意是你能分辨真钞和假钞吗。

collocations.zh: 把一物与另一物区分开

senses.title: To tell two things apart
senses.definition: to see or explain how two things are different
senses.definitionCN: 看出或说明两样东西的不同
senses.example: Children must learn to distinguish fact from opinion.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子必须学会区分事实与看法。
senses.why: Two things only need telling apart when they look alike.
senses.whyCN: 只有长得像的东西，才需要去分辨。

senses.title: To make out with the senses
senses.definition: to manage to see, hear or recognize something faint
senses.definitionCN: 努力看清、听见或认出模糊的东西
senses.example: I could not distinguish her face in the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 在人群里我认不出她的脸。
senses.why: The eye does the same work as the mind, only faster.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛做的和脑子是同一件事，只是更快。

senses.title: To stand out by doing well
senses.definition: to make yourself noticed through good work
senses.definitionCN: 靠出色的表现让人注意到自己
senses.example: He distinguished himself in the final debate.
senses.exampleCN: 他在最后一场辩论中表现突出。
senses.why: One clear mark is enough to lift a name out of the list.
senses.whyCN: 一个清楚的记号，就足以让一个名字从名单里立起来。

intro.en: Distinguish comes from Latin distinguere, to separate by marking, from dis-, apart, and stinguere, to prick.
intro.cn: distinguish 来自拉丁语 distinguere（做记号分开），由 dis-（分开）与 stinguere（刺）构成。

items.en: Stinguere meant to prick or put a mark on something.
items.cn: stinguere 指刺一下或在东西上留记号。

items.en: Dis- carried the marked item away from its neighbours.
items.cn: dis- 把做过记号的那件从旁边的东西里分出来。

items.en: Distinguere grew to mean telling one thing from another.
items.cn: distinguere 逐渐表示把一物与另一物分辨开。

items.en: English used it for seeing a difference.
items.cn: 英语借入时表示看出差别。

items.en: The sense of standing out by merit appeared.
items.cn: 后来出现靠功绩出众的意思。

items.en: Today a good reader distinguishes tone as well as words.
items.cn: 今天好的读者既分辨字面，也分辨语气。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the marking stem, while the meaning group gathers other verbs of telling apart.
note.cn: 形近组共享「做记号」的词干，近义组则是几个表示分辨的动词。

entries.definition: clear and clearly separate
a difference, or high quality
able to be told apart
to show or see a difference
to notice something faint or subtle
to name something correctly

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with two leaves in one hand and end with a name lifted above the crowd.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从掌心里两片叶子开始，落到一个被举到人群之上的名字。

normal.en: Dis- plus stinguish: prick a mark, and the two come apart.
normal.cn: dis 加 stinguish，刺个记号，两者就分开了。

normal.en: A good cook can distinguish salt from sugar by touch.
normal.cn: 好厨子一摸就能分出盐和糖。

normal.en: At dusk you cannot distinguish the path from the grass.
normal.cn: 黄昏时你分不清小路和草地。

normal.en: She distinguished herself in the first round.
normal.cn: 她在第一轮就表现突出。

normal.en: Teachers distinguish effort from talent when they mark.
normal.cn: 老师批改时会区分努力与天赋。

abstract.en: Picture two leaves held up to the light, veins compared.
abstract.cn: 想象两片叶子举到光下比对叶脉。

abstract.en: Picture a mark pricked on one card among many.
abstract.cn: 想象许多卡片中有一张被刺了记号。

abstract.en: Picture one head rising above a seated crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象坐着的人群里有一个头抬得更高。

examples.en: It is hard to distinguish the two shades of blue.
examples.cn: 这两种蓝色很难分辨。

examples.en: She distinguished herself in the school choir.
examples.cn: 她在校合唱团里表现突出。

examples.en: He cannot distinguish left from right without a sign.
examples.cn: 没有标记他就分不清左右。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 distinguish 记成「刺个记号分出来」：dis 表示分开，stingu 来自刺，刺上记号，就能把相似的东西分辨开，做得好还会被单独看见。

root: 源自拉丁语 distinguere，由 dis-（分开）与 stinguere（刺）组成，本义是刺出记号把东西区别开。英语先指看出差别，再指在模糊中辨认出某物，后来引申为靠出色表现让自己被单独看见。

sensesIntro.en: From telling two leaves apart to making your own name stand out of the list.
sensesIntro.cn: 从分辨两片叶子，到让自己的名字从名单里立起来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two look-alike leaves held to the light while the eyes compare their veins.
core.cn: 核心意象：两片相似的叶子举到光下，眼睛比对叶脉。

branches.en: The first sense is the work of telling two things apart.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把两样东西分辨开的工作。

branches.en: The second sense does that work with the senses alone.
branches.cn: 第二个义项只用五官来完成这件事。

branches.en: The third sense turns being noticed into being admired.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把被看见变成被称赞。

branches.en: Both senses need attention to a small difference.
branches.cn: 两个义项都需要留意细微的差别。

branches.en: Both senses depend on a mark that others can see.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖别人看得见的记号。

intro.en: Distinguish belongs to the marking family, where a pricked mark separates and also lifts a name.
intro.cn: distinguish 属于「做记号」一族，一道刺出的记号既能分开东西，也能让一个名字立起来。

latinIntro.en: Latin stinguere, to prick, gives distinguish and distinct; dis- turns one mark into a clear separation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stinguere（刺）给出 distinguish 与 distinct，前缀 dis- 把一个记号变成清楚的分隔。

items.example: Can you distinguish the two inks?
items.exampleCN: 你分得出这两种墨水吗？

items.example: The distinction is easy to miss.
items.exampleCN: 这个区别很容易被忽略。

items.example: Her only distinguishing mark is a scar.
items.exampleCN: 她唯一可辨的标记是一道疤。

definition_zh: 扭曲；使变形；歪曲（事实、意思）；使失真
definition_en: to twist something out of its true shape, or to report it in a way that no longer matches it
core_image: 一张平展的铁皮被钳子拧成螺旋，原本笔直的边成了弯的
scene: 编辑把受访者的两段话剪接在一起，前后颠倒之后，意思完全变了。The editor distorted the interview by joining two separate answers.
sceneCN: 这里指把原话剪接成与本人意思不符的样子（第 2 个义项：歪曲事实或他人的陈述）；句意：编辑把两段互不相干的回答拼在一起，歪曲了这次访谈。

pos.zh: 扭曲；使变形；歪曲；使失真

senses.title: To twist something out of shape
senses.definition: to bend or twist an object so that its natural form is lost
senses.definitionCN: 弯折或拧转物体，使其失去原有形状
senses.example: The heat distorted the plastic casing.
senses.exampleCN: 高温使塑料外壳变形。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to twist apart, so the first sense is the hand's work on a solid object.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为拧开，因此第一个义项是手在固体上做的事。

senses.title: To misrepresent facts or a statement
senses.definition: to report something so that it no longer corresponds to what was said or done
senses.definitionCN: 报道某事时使其不再符合原话或原事
senses.example: The editor distorted the interview by joining two separate answers.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑把两段互不相干的回答拼在一起，歪曲了这次访谈。
senses.why: A report can be bent just as a sheet of metal can, and the same verb covers both.
senses.whyCN: 叙述像铁皮一样可以被弯折，同一个动词两边都管。

senses.title: To alter a signal so it is unfaithful
senses.definition: to change a sound, an image or a waveform so that the copy no longer matches the original
senses.definitionCN: 改变声音、图像或波形，使副本不再与原物相符
senses.example: A cheap amplifier distorts the signal at high volume.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价的放大器在高音量下会使信号失真。
senses.why: Electronics took the physical twist into the invisible: a wave's shape is bent out of truth.
senses.whyCN: 电子学把物理扭曲带进看不见的领域：波形的形状被拧离真实。

senses.title: To bias or skew statistics
senses.definition: to shape the collection or the presentation of data so that a result is pushed one way
senses.definitionCN: 在数据收集或呈现上做手脚，使结果偏向一方
senses.example: Choosing only surviving firms distorts the average.
senses.exampleCN: 只挑选存活下来的公司会使平均值失真。
senses.why: A number can be bent by the way it is gathered, so the verb moves from metal to method.
senses.whyCN: 数字能被采集方式拧弯，于是这个动词从金属转到方法。

senses.title: To distort prices or a market
senses.definition: to change prices or incentives so that they no longer reflect real costs or demand
senses.definitionCN: 改变价格或激励，使其不再反映真实成本或需求
senses.example: Subsidies distort the price of fuel across the region.
senses.exampleCN: 补贴扭曲了整个地区的燃料价格。
senses.why: Economics speaks of distorted signals when the market's information is bent by intervention.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把被干预拧弯的市场信息称为失真的信号。

senses.title: To twist the meaning of words
senses.definition: to give a word or a phrase a sense it does not properly carry
senses.definitionCN: 给一个词或短语安上它本不具备的意思
senses.example: The slogan distorts the meaning of the original promise.
senses.exampleCN: 这句口号把原来承诺的意思拧歪了。
senses.why: Meaning has a shape too, and stretching it until it fits another purpose is the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 意义也有形状，把它拉到另一用途上，用的还是同一个动词。

senses.title: Of metal or plastic under stress
senses.definition: of a material, to change shape permanently under heat or load
senses.definitionCN: 材料在高温或载荷下发生永久形变
senses.example: The beam distorted under the weight of the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 横梁在屋顶的重量下变形了。
senses.why: Engineering keeps the most literal sense and measures how far a part may bend before it fails.
senses.whyCN: 工程学保留最字面的义项，并测量构件在失效前能弯多少。

senses.title: To warp a person's public image
senses.titleCN: 把某人的公众形象写得失真
senses.definition: to present a person's character or motives in a way that exaggerates or invents
senses.definitionCN: 以夸大或编造的方式呈现某人的性格或动机
senses.example: The article distorted her as a careless manager.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇文章把她写成一个粗心的管理者，与实情不符。
senses.why: When the object is a person, the twist becomes a story that others will believe.
senses.whyCN: 当对象是一个人，这种拧转就变成一则别人会相信的故事。

intro.en: Distort comes from a Latin verb meaning to twist apart, built from a prefix of reversal and the verb for twisting. English took it in the sixteenth century, and its sense spread from bodies to reports and signals.
intro.cn: 本词出自一个表示拧开的拉丁动词，由表示反向的前缀与表示拧转的动词构成。英语在十六世纪借入，含义从物体扩展到叙述与信号。

items.en: Torquere meant to twist, and it also stands behind the words for torque and for torture.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为拧、扭，英语中表示转矩与酷刑的词也出自它。

items.en: The prefix meant apart or in different directions, so the compound pictured a twist that pulls a shape open.
items.cn: 这个前缀表示分开或朝不同方向，因此复合词描绘把形状拧开的力量。

items.en: The Latin verb meant to twist awry, and it could describe limbs, metal and speech.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为拧歪，可用于肢体、金属与言辞。

items.en: English borrowed it in the sixteenth century, first for bodies and faces, then for accounts.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入，先用于身体与面孔，再用于叙述。

items.en: Sound engineering and economics later applied the word to waves and to prices.
items.cn: 声学工程与经济学后来把这个词用到波形与价格上。

note.en: The first group shares the twisting root or its English forms; the second group names nearby ways of falsifying. Distort twists a shape or a story out of truth, whereas contaminate mixes something foreign into a clean substance, so bending and adulterating are different acts.
note.cn: 第一组共享拧转词根或其英语形式；第二组是相邻的造假方式。本词把形状或叙述拧离真实，污染类词则把外来物混进洁净之物，弯折与掺混是两种动作。

entries.definition: The bent shape, the false report or the unfaithful signal.
entries.definitionCN: 被弯的形状、失实的报道或失真的信号。

entries.definition: Already twisted out of the true form.
entries.definitionCN: 已经被拧离真实形态的。

entries.definition: The turning force that twists an object; it shares the root but is a technical noun.
entries.definitionCN: 使物体扭转的力矩；共享词根，但是技术名词。

entries.definition: A wrong for which the law gives a remedy, literally something twisted.
entries.definitionCN: 法律给予救济的侵害行为，字面意为被拧歪之事。

entries.definition: To turn something around itself; it can be literal or figurative but names no falsehood.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物绕自身转；可字面可比喻，但不含虚假之意。

entries.definition: To bend out of shape, especially by heat or damp; it stresses material change.
entries.definitionCN: 使变形，尤指受热或受潮；强调材料变化。

entries.definition: To give a false account; the emphasis is on the account rather than the twist.
entries.definitionCN: 作失实叙述；强调叙述，而非拧转。

entries.definition: To bias a result or a view; it is statistics-friendly and less physical.
entries.definitionCN: 使结果或看法偏斜；多用于统计，物理意味较弱。

entries.definition: To make false, often deliberately, as in falsifying records.
entries.definitionCN: 使变假，常指故意，如伪造记录。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the twisting root, the real family and the objects that show the physical and the figurative uses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用拧转词根、真实同族词，以及能显示字面与比喻用法的宾语。

normal.en: The root means to twist, so the verb is a twist that pulls a form away from its truth.
normal.cn: 词根意为拧，动词就是把形状拧离真实的动作。

normal.en: The family runs distortion, distorted, distortive and the technical distortionless.
normal.cn: 同族词有失真、扭曲的、造成扭曲的，以及技术用语无失真的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: distort the facts, distort the meaning, distort prices.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：歪曲事实、歪曲含义、扭曲价格。

normal.en: Electronics gives the invisible version: a wave bent away from its true shape.
normal.cn: 电子学给出看不见的版本：波形被拧离本形。

normal.en: The look-alike nouns for torque and for a legal wrong share the same twisting root.
normal.cn: 表示转矩与法律侵害的形近名词共享同一个拧转词根。

abstract.en: Picture a straight ruler held at both ends and slowly bent into an arc.
abstract.cn: 想象一把直尺两端被握住，慢慢弯成弧形。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour that grows a new detail each time it is retold.
abstract.cn: 想象一则传言每被转述一次就多出一个细节。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow stretched sideways until it no longer resembles the body.
abstract.cn: 想象影子被横向拉长，直到不再像原来的身体。

examples.en: The lens distorted the straight lines near the edge of the photo.
examples.cn: 镜头使照片边缘附近的直线变形。

examples.en: Both sides accused the other of distorting the record.
examples.cn: 双方都指责对方歪曲记录。

examples.en: A small sample can distort the overall picture.
examples.cn: 样本过小会使整体情况失真。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迪」加「斯托特」——把铁皮拧成麻花，形状和意思都走样：扭曲、歪曲

root: 拉丁语「分开」前缀加「拧转」动词构成「拧歪」，十六世纪进入英语；从身体与面孔扩展到叙述、信号与价格。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all bend a form away from its truth: an object, a report, a signal, a statistic, a price, a word, a loaded beam and a public image.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把某种形态拧离真实：物体、报道、信号、统计、价格、词语、受载的梁与公众形象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat sheet of metal gripped by pliers and twisted into a spiral, its straight edge now curved.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张平展的铁皮被钳子拧成螺旋，原本笔直的边成了弯的。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL: an object twisted by heat, and a beam bent under load.
branches.cn: 材料：被高温拧变形的物体，以及受载弯曲的梁。

branches.en: THE ACCOUNT: facts misreported, and a person's image warped into a story.
branches.cn: 叙述：被失实报道的事实，以及被写成故事的公众形象。

branches.en: THE SIGNAL: a wave or image that no longer matches the original.
branches.cn: 信号：不再与原物相符的波形或图像。

branches.en: THE NUMBER AND THE PRICE: statistics pushed one way and market signals bent by intervention.
branches.cn: 数字与价格：被推向一方的统计，以及被干预拧弯的市场信号。

branches.en: THE WORD: a meaning stretched until it serves another purpose.
branches.cn: 词语：被拉到另一用途上的意义。

intro.en: Distort is a Latin verb of twisting, and its family supplies the noun of the bent shape and the adjective of what has been bent.
intro.cn: 本词是一个表示拧转的拉丁动词，其词族提供表示被弯形状的名词，以及描述已被弯折之物的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin torquere and the prefix of reversal form the verb; the noun came into English through the Latin noun of the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示拧转的动词与表示反向的前缀构成这个动词；名词则经同一词干的拉丁名词进入英语。

items.example: It turns the twist into a twist away from the true form.
items.exampleCN: 它把拧转变成拧离本形。

items.example: The root supplies the physical act.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供这个物理动作。

items.example: The verb is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: English kept a shortened form of the Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留了拉丁动词的缩短形式。

items.example: It builds the noun for the bent shape or the false report.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示被弯形状或失实报道的名词。

items.example: It marks the object after the twist.
items.exampleCN: 它标记被拧过之后的对象。

items.example: It builds the rare adjective for what causes distortion.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示造成扭曲的罕见形容词。

items.example: It builds the technical adjective for a faithful signal.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示信号不失真的技术形容词。

items.example: The same root survived as a mechanical noun.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根作为机械名词留存下来。

definition_zh: n. 变形；扭曲；曲解；失真
definition_en: a change that makes something bent out of its true shape, meaning or quality
core_image: 直尺透过玻璃碗看上去弯了；两段回答被剪接成一句误导的话；平滑波形上长出锯齿；天平一端被拇指压住

senses.title: Bent out of shape
senses.definition: a change that makes something bent out of its true shape
senses.definitionCN: （名词）使某物偏离真实形状的变化
senses.example: The lens causes distortion at the edges of the photo.
senses.exampleCN: 镜头使照片边缘产生畸变。
senses.why: A straight ruler looking curved through a glass bowl.
senses.whyCN: 透过玻璃碗看上去弯了的直尺。

senses.title: A twisted account
senses.definition: a false account that twists what was said or happened
senses.definitionCN: （名词）把说过的话或发生过的事拧歪的虚假陈述
senses.example: The report is a distortion of the facts.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇报道是对事实的曲解。
senses.why: Two separate answers spliced into one misleading sentence.
senses.whyCN: 两段独立回答被剪接成一句误导的话。

senses.title: Spoiled signal
senses.definition: a change that spoils the quality of a sound or image
senses.definitionCN: （名词）损害声音或图像质量的变化
senses.example: There is distortion in the recording.
senses.exampleCN: 这段录音里有失真。
senses.why: A smooth wave drawn with jagged teeth on top.
senses.whyCN: 一条平滑波形上长出锯齿。

senses.title: A misleading skew
senses.definition: a skew that makes results or prices misleading
senses.definitionCN: （名词）使结果或价格产生误导的偏斜
senses.example: The subsidy creates a distortion in the market.
senses.exampleCN: 补贴造成市场扭曲。

senses.whyCN: 一架被拇指压住一端托盘的天平。
